problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\sqrt{3}\,k.$

feedback.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t,\,\frac{1}{t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨2,\,2(1),\,\frac{1}{1}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(2)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+1} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
